No for the most part, an actual Ketogenic diet has specific macro ratios to keep glycogen level low. The general ratio of macros to follow is 70% fats, 25% protein, and 5% carbohydrates in a keto diet. A high protein, high fat, and low carb paleo is not always a keto diet. Having too much protein will cause glycogen levels to increase and will kick the body out of ketosis.

The reason is that a body can get glycogen in two ways:

The one that is most common today is the breakdown of carbs to glycogen, it is the reason most people believe you need carbs to do endurance sports. This is where people get the idea that you're supposed to carb load before a race.

The other one that runners like Zach Bitter use is getting glycogen from excess protein this process is called Gluconeogenesis and provides glycogen to the body from mostly the liver.

In my opinion there's no real benefits to be in ketosis all the time unless it's for medical reasons like seizure prevention.
